questions.q: Muscle contraction is initiated by a signal sent by the central nervous system through the release of __________.
questions.solution:
Muscle contraction is initiated by a signal sent by the central nervous system (CNS) via a motor neuron.

When the neural signal reaches the neuromuscular junction or motor end plate, it triggers the release of a neurotransmitter called acetylcholine.

Acetylcholine binds to receptors on the sarcolemma, generating an action potential that spreads through the muscle fibre and causes the release of calcium ions into the sarcoplasm, thereby initiating muscle contraction.

Answer: acetyl choline

questions.q: The parts of human brain that helps in regulation of sexual behaviour, expression of excitement, pleaseure, rage, fear, etc. are:
questions.solution:
The cerebrum wraps around a structure called thalamus, which is a major coordinating centre for sensory and motor signaling. The hypothalamus lies at the base of the thalamus.

The hypothalamus contains a number of centres which control body temperature, urge for eating and drinking, along with secretion of hypothalamic hormones.

The inner parts of cerebral hemispheres and a group of associated deep structures like amygdala, hippocampus, etc., form a complex structure called the limbic lobe or limbic system. questions.solution:
Mechanism of vision: In the dark photoreceptors release an inhibitory neurotransmitter that prevents the activation of ganglion cells by bipolar neurons. Light inhibits the photoreceptors from releasing the inhibitory transmitter. Without this inhibition, the bipolar neurons are able to stimulate the ganglion cells. The ganglion cells transmit action cortex analyses and compare the input with earlier stored experiences for understanding the input (image).
The photoreceptors contain many Na+ channels in their plasma membrane. In the dark these channels are open and Na+ ions enter inducing depolarization of photoreceptors and release of inhibitory neurotransmitters. In the light, the photopigments present in the receptors become converted from 11-cis-retinene to all –trans-retinene. The trans-retinene gets dissociated from opsin protein. This brings up the closing of Ca+2 channels and opens up of Na+ channels and the potential gradient is formed. The photoreceptors do not release the inhibitory neurotransmitter hence, the bipolar neurons release excitatory neurotransmitters stimulating ganglion cells.

Impulse transmission across a chemical synapse is always faster than that across an electrical synapse
The membranes of presynaptic and postsynaptic neurons are ibn close proximity in an electrical synapse
questions.solution:
The major difference between a chemical and an electrical synapse is that in a chemical synapse, the nerve impulse is transmitted chemically via neurotransmitters, whereas in an electrical synapse a nerve impulse is transmitted electrically via channel proteins.

Chemical synapses use the release of chemical neurotransmitters to propagate signals from one neuron (presynaptic) to another (postsynaptic). The electrical synapses are specialised connections between neurons that facilitate direct ionic and small metabolite communication. Hence, the electrical synapses are very faster and are found in all nervous systems, especially in the human brain.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Which of the following statement is coorect?
(i) The rods contain a purplish-red protein called the rhodopsin.
(ii) The photopigments are embedded in the membrane discs of the inner segment.
(iii) Retinal is a derivative of vitamin A.
(iv) Light induces dissociation of the retinal from opsin resulting in changes in the structure of the opsin.
questions.solution:
The inner layer of an eye is the retina, and it contains three layers of neural cells — from inside to outside — ganglion cells, bipolar cells and photoreceptor cells. There are two types of photoreceptor cells, namely, rods and cones. These cells contain the light-sensitive proteins called the photopigments. The daylight (photopic) vision and colour vision are functions of cones and the twilight (scotopic) vision is the function of the rods. The rods contain a purplish-red protein called the rhodopsin or visual purple, which contains a derivative of Vitamin A.

Mechanism of Vision

The light rays in visible wavelength focussed on the retina through the cornea and lens generate potentials (impulses) in rods and cones. As mentioned earlier, the photosensitive compounds (photopigments) in the human eyes is composed of opsin (a protein) and retinal (an aldehyde of vitamin A). Light induces dissociation of the retinal from opsin resulting in changes in the structure of the opsin. This causes membrane permeability changes. As a result, potential differences are generated in the photoreceptor cells. This produces a signal that generates action potentials in the ganglion cells through the bipolar cells. These action potentials (impulses) are transmitted by the optic nerves to the visual cortex area of the brain, where the neural impulses are analysed and the image formed on the retina is recognised based on earlier memory and experience.

Carotene is the source of retinal which is involved in the formation of rhodopsin of rod cells.

The process by which two or more organs interact and complement each other's functions.

questions.solution: Coordination refers to the process by which two or more organs interact and complement each other's functions in order to maintain homeostasis. When physical exercise is performed, the supply of oxygen increases to meet the increased energy demand. When physical exercise is stopped, the activities of nerves, lungs, heart and kidney gradually return to their normal conditions. The neural system and the endocrine system jointly coordinate and integrate all the activities of the organs so that they function in a synchronised fashion. The neural system provides an organized network of point-to-point connections for quick coordination. The endocrine system provides chemical integration through hormones.

options: The membrane is in a depolarised state.

questions.solution: Similarly, the membrane is impermeable to negatively charged proteins present in the axoplasm. Consequently, the axoplasm inside the axon contains high concentration of K+ and negatively charged proteins and low concentration of Na+. In contrast, the fluid outside the axon contains a low concentration of K+, a high concentration of Na+ and thus form a concentration gradient. These ionic gradients across the resting membrane are maintained by the active transport of ions by the sodium-potassium pump which transports 3 Na+ outwards for 2 K+ into the cell. As a result, the outer surface of the axonal membrane possesses a positive charge while its inner surface becomes negatively charged and therefore is polarised. The electrical potential difference across the resting plasma membrane is called as the resting potential. The electrical potential difference across the plasma membrane at the site A is called the action potential, which is in fact termed as a nerve impulse. At sites immediately ahead, the axon (e.g., site B) membrane has a positive charge on the outer surface and a negative charge on its inner surface. As a result, a current flows on the inner surface from site A to site B. On the outer surface current flows from site B to site A to complete the circuit of current flow. Hence, the polarity at the site is reversed, and an action potential is generated at site B. Thus, the impulse (action potential) generated at site A arrives at site B. The sequence is repeated along the length of the axon and consequently the impulse is conducted. The rise in the stimulus-induced permeability to Na+ is extremely short lived. It is quickly followed by a rise in permeability to K+. Within a fraction of a second, K+ diffuses outside the membrane and restores the resting potential of the membrane at the site of excitation and the fibre becomes once more responsive to further stimulation.

questions.solution: A nerve impulse is transmitted from one neuron to another through junctions called synapses. A synapse is formed by the membranes of a pre-synaptic neuron and a post-synaptic neuron, which may or may not be separated by a gap called synaptic cleft. There are two types of synapses, namely, electrical synapses and chemical synapses. At electrical synapses, the membranes of pre- and post-synaptic neurons are in very close proximity. Electrical current can flow directly from one neuron into the other across these synapses. Transmission of an impulse across electrical synapses is very similar to impulse conduction along a single axon. Impulse transmission across an electrical synapse is always faster than that across a chemical synapse. Electrical synapses are rare in our system. Chemicals called neurotransmitters are involved in the transmission of impulses at these synapses. The axon terminals contain vesicles filled with these neurotransmitters. When an impulse (action potential) arrives at the axon terminal, it stimulates the movement of the synaptic vesicles towards the membrane where they fuse with the plasma membrane and release their neurotransmitters in the synaptic cleft. The released neurotransmitters bind to their specific receptors, present on the post-synaptic membrane. Assertion (A): In a chemical synapse, neurotransmitters are released only from the pre-synaptic terminal and their specific receptors are present only on the post-synaptic membrane.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

Both Assertion and Reason are correct but Reason is not the correct explanation for Assertion.

questions.solution:
In a chemical synapse, synaptic vesicles containing neurotransmitters are located only in the pre-synaptic terminal, and specific receptors for these neurotransmitters are located exclusively on the post-synaptic membrane. Thus, the Assertion is correct.

This structural asymmetry ensures that a nerve impulse can only travel in one direction (from the pre-synaptic to the post-synaptic neuron). Thus, the Reason is also correct.

However, the structural arrangement (Assertion) is the cause of the unidirectional transmission (Reason). The Reason is the functional consequence, not the explanation, of the Assertion. Therefore, both Assertion and Reason are correct, but Reason is not the correct explanation for Assertion.

Answer: Both Assertion and Reason are correct but Reason is not the correct explanation for Assertion.

options: Both Assertion and Reason are correct and Reason is the correct explanation for Assertion.
Both Assertion and Reason are correct but Reason is not the correct explanation for Assertion.
Assertion is correct but Reason is incorrect.
Assertion is incorrect but Reason is correct.
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is incorrect because the correct sequence of the cranial meninges from the outside to the inside is: outer dura mater, middle arachnoid, and inner pia mater.

Reason (R) is correct as the human brain is indeed well protected by the cranial meninges located inside the skull.

Therefore, the Assertion is incorrect but the Reason is correct.

Answer: Assertion is incorrect but Reason is correct.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements carefully:
I. Electrical synapses are rare in the human neural system.
II. At chemical synapses, the arriving action potential stimulates the movement of synaptic vesicles towards the membrane.
III. Neurotransmitters bind to specific receptors located on the presynaptic membrane.
IV. A fluid-filled space called the synaptic cleft is always absent in chemical synapses.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement I is correct as electrical synapses are rare in our neural system.

Statement II is correct because the arrival of an action potential at the axon terminal stimulates synaptic vesicles to move towards and fuse with the plasma membrane.

Statement III is incorrect because the specific receptors for neurotransmitters are located on the post-synaptic membrane, not the presynaptic membrane.

Statement IV is incorrect because the membranes of pre- and post-synaptic neurons at a chemical synapse are separated by a fluid-filled space called the synaptic cleft.

Therefore, exactly two statements (I and II) are correct.

Answer: Two

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): All the muscle fibres innervated by a single motor neuron contract simultaneously when a signal is sent by the central nervous system.

Reason (R): The motor neuron releases acetylcholine at the neuromuscular junctions of all the muscle fibres it innervates upon receiving an action potential.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.solution:
A motor neuron along with all the muscle fibres connected to it constitute a motor unit. When an action potential from the central nervous system reaches the axon terminals of the motor neuron, it simultaneously releases the neurotransmitter acetylcholine at all the neuromuscular junctions it forms.

This generates an action potential in the sarcolemma of all these connected muscle fibres at the same time, leading to their simultaneous contraction. Therefore, both the Assertion and the Reason are correct, and the Reason correctly explains the Assertion.

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: During the transmission of a nerve impulse across a chemical synapse, what is the immediate physiological consequence of neurotransmitters binding to their specific receptors on the post-synaptic membrane?
options: Movement of synaptic vesicles towards the pre-synaptic membrane
Release of neurotransmitters into the synaptic cleft
Generation of an action potential in the pre-synaptic neuron
questions.solution:
During synaptic transmission at a chemical synapse, the binding of neurotransmitters to their specific receptors on the post-synaptic membrane leads to the opening of specific ion channels.

This opening allows the entry of ions, which can generate a new potential (either excitatory or inhibitory) in the post-synaptic neuron.

The movement of synaptic vesicles and the release of neurotransmitters are pre-synaptic events that occur prior to receptor binding, while the action potential in the pre-synaptic neuron is the initial trigger for the entire process.

Answer: Opening of specific ion channels

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: A specific type of synapse 'X' allows the direct flow of electrical current from one neuron to another, resulting in an impulse transmission that is always faster than that across other synapse types. Identify synapse 'X' and its relative abundance in the human neural system.
questions.solution:
At an electrical synapse, the membranes of pre- and post-synaptic neurons are in very close proximity, allowing electrical current to flow directly from one neuron into the other. This direct flow makes impulse transmission across an electrical synapse always faster than that across a chemical synapse. However, according to NCERT, electrical synapses are rare in the human neural system. Therefore, synapse 'X' is an electrical synapse and it is rare.

Answer: Electrical synapse; Rare

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements carefully:
I. Unipolar neurons possess a cell body with one axon only and are typically found in the embryonic stage.
II. Bipolar neurons possess one axon and two or more dendrites and are found in the cerebral cortex.
III. Myelinated nerve fibres are commonly found in the autonomous and somatic neural systems.
IV. Unmyelinated nerve fibres are enclosed by a Schwann cell that does not form a myelin sheath around the axon.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement I is correct: Unipolar neurons have a cell body with one axon only and are found usually in the embryonic stage.

Statement II is incorrect: Bipolar neurons possess one axon and one dendrite and are found in the retina of the eye. Multipolar neurons possess one axon and two or more dendrites and are found in the cerebral cortex.

Statement III is incorrect: Myelinated nerve fibres are found in spinal and cranial nerves. Unmyelinated nerve fibres are commonly found in the autonomous and somatic neural systems.

Statement IV is correct: Unmyelinated nerve fibres are enclosed by a Schwann cell that does not form a myelin sheath around the axon.

Therefore, exactly two statements (I and IV) are correct.

Answer: Two

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: During the initiation of muscle contraction, a neural signal triggers the release of the neurotransmitter acetylcholine into the synaptic cleft. The specific receptors for acetylcholine are located on the:
questions.solution:
At the neuromuscular junction (motor end plate), the arrival of a neural signal causes the release of the neurotransmitter acetylcholine from the motor neuron into the synaptic cleft.

Acetylcholine diffuses across the cleft and binds to its specific receptors, which are located on the sarcolemma (the plasma membrane of the muscle fibre). This binding generates an action potential in the sarcolemma that spreads through the muscle fibre.

The sarcoplasmic reticulum is the internal storehouse for calcium ions. Synaptic vesicles are located in the axon terminal and store the neurotransmitter. Troponin is a regulatory protein on the actin filament that binds calcium ions, not acetylcholine.

Answer: Sarcolemma

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements (A) to (E) carefully:
(A) Unipolar neurons possess a cell body with one axon only and are usually found in the embryonic stage.
(B) Bipolar neurons have one axon and two or more dendrites and are found in the retina of the eye.
(C) Multipolar neurons are found in the cerebral cortex.
(D) Schwann cells form a myelin sheath around the axon in all types of nerve fibres.
(E) The synaptic knob possesses synaptic vesicles containing neurotransmitters.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement (A) is correct as unipolar neurons have a cell body with one axon only and are found in the embryonic stage.

Statement (B) is incorrect because bipolar neurons have one axon and exactly one dendrite, not two or more dendrites.

Statement (C) is correct as multipolar neurons (one axon and two or more dendrites) are found in the cerebral cortex.

Statement (D) is incorrect because while Schwann cells enclose unmyelinated nerve fibres as well, they do not form a myelin sheath around the axon in unmyelinated nerve fibres.

Statement (E) is correct as the synaptic knob contains synaptic vesicles filled with neurotransmitters.

Therefore, exactly three statements (A, C, and E) are correct.

Answer: Three

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following options correctly identifies the sequence of structural descriptions for the primary neural tissues found in the embryonic stage, the cerebral cortex, and the somatic neural system, respectively?
options: Cell body with one axon only ; One axon and two or more dendrites ; Enclosed by a Schwann cell that does not form a myelin sheath
One axon and two or more dendrites ; Cell body with one axon only ; Enclosed by a Schwann cell that does not form a myelin sheath
Cell body with one axon only ; One axon and one dendrite ; Enclosed by a Schwann cell that does not form a myelin sheath
Cell body with one axon only ; One axon and two or more dendrites ; Enveloped with Schwann cells forming a myelin sheath
questions.solution:
The question requires mapping anatomical locations directly to their structural definitions based on NCERT:

1. Embryonic stage: Neurons here are typically unipolar, defined structurally as having a cell body with one axon only.
2. Cerebral cortex: Neurons here are multipolar, defined structurally as having one axon and two or more dendrites.
3. Somatic neural system: Nerve fibres here are unmyelinated, defined structurally as being enclosed by a Schwann cell that does not form a myelin sheath around the axon.

Option 1 correctly lists these structural descriptions in the requested order.
Option 2 is incorrect because it swaps the structures of the embryonic stage and the cerebral cortex.
Option 3 is incorrect because it describes the cerebral cortex neuron as bipolar (one axon and one dendrite), which is actually found in the retina of the eye.
Option 4 is incorrect because it describes the somatic neural system as having myelinated nerve fibres, which are instead found in spinal and cranial nerves.

Answer: Cell body with one axon only ; One axon and two or more dendrites ; Enclosed by a Schwann cell that does not form a myelin sheath

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following events that occur during the initiation of muscle contraction:

(A) Release of acetylcholine into the synaptic cleft
(B) Arrival of neural signal at the axon terminal of a motor neuron
(C) Generation of an action potential in the sarcolemma
(D) Binding of neurotransmitter to receptors on the motor end plate
(E) Release of calcium ions from the sarcoplasmic reticulum

Choose the correct chronological sequence of these events.
questions.solution:
Muscle contraction is initiated by a signal sent by the central nervous system via a motor neuron. The correct sequence of events is as follows:

First, the neural signal arrives at the axon terminal of the motor neuron (B).

This triggers the synaptic vesicles to release the neurotransmitter acetylcholine into the synaptic cleft (A).

Acetylcholine then binds to its specific receptors present on the motor end plate (D).

This binding generates an action potential in the sarcolemma (C).

The action potential spreads through the muscle fibre, causing the release of calcium ions from the sarcoplasmic reticulum into the sarcoplasm (E).

Therefore, the correct chronological sequence is (B) → (A) → (D) → (C) → (E).

Answer: (B) → (A) → (D) → (C) → (E)

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Consider two types of nerve fibres in the human neural system: Fibre A is extracted from a cranial nerve, and Fibre B is extracted from a nerve of the autonomous neural system.

Which of the following correctly describes the primary structural difference between Fibre A and Fibre B regarding their coverings?
options: Fibre A is enclosed by Schwann cells, whereas Fibre B completely lacks Schwann cells.
Fibre B possesses a myelin sheath, whereas Fibre A does not.
Both fibres possess a myelin sheath, but Fibre B lacks nodes of Ranvier.
Fibre A has a myelin sheath formed by Schwann cells, whereas Fibre B is enclosed by Schwann cells but lacks a myelin sheath.
questions.solution:
According to NCERT, cranial nerves contain myelinated nerve fibres, whereas the autonomous neural system contains unmyelinated nerve fibres.

Myelinated nerve fibres (Fibre A) are enveloped with Schwann cells which form a myelin sheath around the axon.

Unmyelinated nerve fibres (Fibre B) are also enclosed by a Schwann cell, but this cell does not form a myelin sheath around the axon.

Therefore, Fibre A has a myelin sheath formed by Schwann cells, while Fibre B is enclosed by Schwann cells but lacks a myelin sheath. Options suggesting Fibre B lacks Schwann cells entirely or possesses a myelin sheath are incorrect.

Answer: Fibre A has a myelin sheath formed by Schwann cells, whereas Fibre B is enclosed by Schwann cells but lacks a myelin sheath.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Match List I with List II regarding synapses.

List IList II
(A) Fluid-filled space called synaptic cleft(I) Electrical synapse
(B) Membranes are in very close proximity(II) Chemical synapse
(C) Slower impulse transmission
(D) Rare in our system

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
At a chemical synapse, the membranes of the pre- and post-synaptic neurons are separated by a fluid-filled space called the synaptic cleft. Impulse transmission across a chemical synapse is slower compared to an electrical synapse.

At electrical synapses, the membranes of pre- and post-synaptic neurons are in very close proximity, allowing direct flow of electrical current, making transmission faster. Electrical synapses are rare in the human neural system.

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(II), (B)-(I), (C)-(II), and (D)-(I).

Answer: (A)-(II), (B)-(I), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Suppose a neuron found in the human embryonic stage were to structurally mature into a typical neuron of the cerebral cortex. Which of the following describes the primary morphological change it must undergo?
options: It would develop one additional axon and multiple dendrites.
It would develop exactly one dendrite while retaining its single axon.
It would develop one additional dendrite, assuming it already possesses one.
It would develop two or more dendrites while retaining its single axon.
questions.solution:
According to NCERT, neurons in the embryonic stage are typically unipolar, which means they consist of a cell body with one axon only and lack dendrites.

Neurons in the cerebral cortex are multipolar, meaning they possess one axon and two or more dendrites.

Therefore, to transition from an embryonic (unipolar) neuron to a cerebral cortex (multipolar) neuron, the cell must develop two or more dendrites while retaining its single axon.

Option 1 is incorrect because multipolar neurons have only one axon.
Option 2 is incorrect because developing exactly one dendrite would result in a bipolar neuron (found in the retina of the eye).
Option 3 is incorrect because embryonic neurons are unipolar and do not already possess a dendrite.

Answer: It would develop two or more dendrites while retaining its single axon.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: In a chemical synapse, which of the following is characteristically localized on the post-synaptic membrane?
questions.solution:
In a chemical synapse, the pre-synaptic neuron transmits the signal by releasing neurotransmitters from synaptic vesicles into the synaptic cleft.

These neurotransmitters then bind to specific receptors which are exclusively located on the post-synaptic membrane.

Synaptic vesicles are found in the pre-synaptic terminal, Schwann cells form the myelin sheath on axons, and Nissl's granules are present in the cell body and dendrites.

Answer: Specific receptors for neurotransmitters

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Match the cranial meninges in List-I with their correct descriptions in List-II.

List-IList-II
(A) Dura mater(I) Middle thin layer
(B) Arachnoid(II) Inner layer in contact with brain tissue
(C) Pia mater(III) Outer thick layer

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
The brain is protected by cranial meninges, which are made up of three layers.

The outermost layer is the dura mater, which is a thick and tough membrane.

The middle layer is the arachnoid, which is a very thin layer.

The innermost layer is the pia mater, which remains in contact with the brain tissue.

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(II).

Answer: (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(II)

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: A specific neuron is observed in the neural layer of the human retina. Identify the structural classification of this neuron and the correct sequence of structures through which a nerve impulse travels within it.
options: Multipolar ; Dendrite → Cell body → Axon → Synaptic knob
Bipolar ; Dendrite → Cell body → Axon → Synaptic knob
Bipolar ; Axon → Cell body → Dendrite → Synaptic knob
Unipolar ; Cell body → Axon → Synaptic knob
questions.solution:
Neurons found in the retina of the eye are structurally classified as bipolar neurons, which possess one axon and one dendrite.

The normal physiological direction of nerve impulse conduction within a single neuron is unidirectional. The impulse is received by the dendrites, travels towards the cell body (cyton), and then passes away from the cell body along the axon to the synaptic knob.

Therefore, the correct classification is bipolar, and the conduction pathway is Dendrite → Cell body → Axon → Synaptic knob.

Answer: Bipolar ; Dendrite → Cell body → Axon → Synaptic knob

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) is present in the subarachnoid space of the human central neural system. Based on the anatomical sequence of the cranial meninges, this space is located between which of the following two layers?
questions.solution:
The cranial meninges consist of three layers: the outer dura mater, the middle arachnoid, and the inner pia mater.

The term "subarachnoid" indicates a position beneath the arachnoid layer. Therefore, the subarachnoid space lies between the middle layer (arachnoid) and the innermost layer (pia mater).

The space between the dura mater and arachnoid is the subdural space, while the space between the cranium (skull) and dura mater is the epidural space.

Answer: Arachnoid and Pia mater

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Match List I with List II regarding the components of a synapse:

List I List II
A. Synaptic vesicles 1. Contains specific receptors for neurotransmitters
B. Synaptic cleft 2. Fluid-filled space between neurons
C. Post-synaptic membrane 3. Pre- and post-synaptic membranes are in very close proximity
D. Electrical synapse 4. Store neurotransmitters

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Synaptic vesicles are found in the pre-synaptic axon terminal and store neurotransmitters (A-4).

The synaptic cleft is the fluid-filled space that separates the pre-synaptic and post-synaptic neurons in a chemical synapse (B-2).

The post-synaptic membrane contains specific receptors that bind to the released neurotransmitters (C-1).

In an electrical synapse, the membranes of pre- and post-synaptic neurons are in very close proximity, allowing direct flow of electric current (D-3).

Therefore, the correct matching is A-4, B-2, C-1, D-3.

Answer: A-4, B-2, C-1, D-3

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Match List I with List II: 

List I

List II
A. Fovea I.  Visible coloured portion of eye that regulates diameter of pupil.
B. Iris II.  External layer of eye formed of dense connective tissue.
C. Blind spot III. Point of greatest visual acuity or resolution.
D. Sclera IV. Point where optic nerve leaves the eyeball and photoreceptor cells are absent

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Fovea
  • At the posterior pole of the eye lateral to the blind spot, there is a yellowish pigmented spot called macula lutea with a central pit called the fovea.
  • The fovea is a thinned-out portion of the retina where only the cones are densely packed. It is the point where the resolution is the greatest.
Iris
  • The continuation of the ciliary body forward to form a pigmented and opaque structure called the iris which is the visible coloured portion of the eye.
Blind spot
  • The optic nerves leave the eye and the retinal blood vessels enter it at a point medial to and slightly above the posterior pole of the eyeball. 
  • Photoreceptor cells are not present in that region and hence it is called the blind spot.
Sclera
  • The external layer or our eye is composed of a dense connective tissue and is called the sclera, which has cornea, choroid and retina.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Stimulation of a muscle fiber by a motor neuron occurs at:
questions.solution: Stimulation of a muscle fiber, by a motor neuron, occurs at the sarcolemma of neuro-muscular junction due to the release of a neurotransmitter (acetylcholine).

questions.solution: A-receptor, B-synaptic cleft, C-synaptic vesicles and $D-\mathrm{Ca}^{2+}$.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The nerve centres which control the body temperature and the urge for eating are contained in
questions.solution: Hypothalamus is the part of the sides and floor of the brain derived from the forebrain. It lies at the base of thalamus. The hypothalamus contains a number of centres, which control body temperature, urge for eating and drinking. It also contains several groups of neurosecretory cells, which secrete hormones called, hypothalamic hormones.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which part of human brain is concerned with the regulation of body temperature ?
questions.solution: No Solution Available

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: During the propagation of a nerve impulse, the action potential results from the movement of
options: $\mathrm{K}^{+}$ions from extracellular fluid to intracellular fluid
$\mathrm{Na}^{+}$ions from intracellular fluid to extracellular fluid
$\mathrm{K}^{+}$ions from intracellular fluid to extracellular fluid
$\mathrm{Na}^{+}$ions from extracellular fluid to intracellular fluid
questions.solution: During the propagation of nerve impulse when a stimulus of adequate strength is applied to a polarised membrane, the permeability of the membrane to $\mathrm{Na}^{+}$is greatly increased at the point of stimulation. As a result the sodium ion channels permit the influx of $\mathrm{Na}^{+}$by diffusion. Since, there are more $\mathrm{Na}^{+}$ions entering than leaving, the electrical potential of the membrane changes from $-70 \mathrm{mV}$ towards zero. At $0 \mathrm{mV}$ the membrane is said to be depolarised. While the resting potential is determined largely by $\mathrm{K}^{+}$ions, the action potential is determined largely by $\mathrm{Na}^{+}$ions. Action potential is another name of nerve impulse. The stimulated negatively charged point on the outside of the membrane sends out an electrical current to the positive point adjacent to it. This local current causes the adjacent inner part of the membrane to reverse its potential from $-70 \mathrm{mV}$ to $+30 \mathrm{mV}$.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Cornea transplant in humans is almost never rejected. This is because
options: its cells are least penetrable by bacteria
it is composed of enucleated cells
questions.solution: Cornea is a transparent portion that forms the anterior one-sixth of the eyeball. The cornea admits and helps to focus light waves as they enter the eye. It is avascular, $i e$, has no blood supply therefore, cornea transplant in human is almost never rejected.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which one of the following is the correct difference between Rod Cells and Cone Cells of our retina?
questions.solution: Rod cells are more concentrated towards the periphery. Visual acuity is highest in fovea centralis which contains only cones. Visual pigment in rods cells is rhodopsin, whereas in the cone cells it is iodopsin.

questions.q: During the propagation of a nerve impulse, the action potential results from the movement of
options: $\mathrm{Na}^{+}$ions from extracellular fluid to intracellular fluid
$\mathrm{Ka}^{+}$ions from extracellular fluid to intracellular fluid
$\mathrm{Na}^{+}$ions from intracellular fluid to extracellular fluid
$\mathrm{Ka}^{+}$ions from intracellular fluid to extracellular fluid

Voltage gated sodium ion channels open and $\mathrm{Na}^{+}$ion flows form extracellular fluid to intracellular fluid, the outside becomes negative and inside positive. The membrane is depolarised \& when the two ends of this membrane is connected to oscilloscope a potential difference of $+30 \mathrm{mv}$, called as action potential is generated.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: During the transmission of nerve impulse through a nerve fibre, the potential on the inner side of the plasma membrane has which type of electric change?
options: first positive, then negative and continue to be negative
first negative, then positive and continue to be positive
first positive, then negative and again back to positive
first negative, then positive and again back to negative.
questions.solution: The first channels to open are the sodium ion channels, which allow sodium ions to enter the cell. The resulting increase in positive charge inside the cell (up to about +40 $\mathrm{mV}$ ) starts the action potential. This is called the depolarization of the membrane. Potassium ion channels Related Theory Events that characterize the transmission of a nerve impulse. (Ref. to Fig. 25.7)

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following is an example of negative feedback loop in humans?
options: secretion of tears after falling of sand particles into the eye
salivation of mouth at the sight of delicious food
secretion of sweat glands and constriction of skin blood vessels when it is too hot
constriction of skin blood vessels and contraction of skeletal muscles when it is too cold.
questions.solution:
When the set point of hypothalamus is disturbed by high temperature, it stimulates vasodilation and sweating while in low temperature there is vasoconstriction and shivering.
Related Theory
Feedback loops are used extensively to regulate secretion of hormones in the hypothalamic-pituitary axis. An important example of a negative feedback loop is seen in control of thyroid hormone secretion. The thyroid hormones thyroxine and triiodothyronine (" $T_4$ and $T_3$ ") are synthesized and secreted by thyroid glands and affect metabolism throughout the body.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of structures distinguishes a nerve cell from other types of cell?
questions.solution:
A nerve cell consists of cell body (perikaryon) containing the nucleus, Nissl granules, dendrites and an axon. These are specialised cells meant for the transmission of the nerve.
Related Theory
The main functions of the myelin sheath in neuron are:
(I) It acts as an electrical insulator for the neuron.
(2) The sheath prevents the movement of ions into or out of the neuron, thus preventing depolarisation.
(3) It speeds up transmission of an electrical impulse in the neuron - impulses cannot travel through the sheath (the sheath acts as an electrical insulator), instead, impulses 'jump' from a gap in the myelin sheath to another gap (it jumps from one Node of Ranvier to another Node). This is a process called Saltatory Conduction.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which one of the following statements is correct?
options: endocrine glands regulate neural activity, but not vice versa
neurons regulate endocrine activity, but not vice versa
endocrine glands regulate neural activity, and nervous system regulates endocrine glands
neither hormones control neural activity nor the neurons control endocrine activity
questions.solution:
The nervous system and endocrine system both use chemical messengers to signal cells, but each has a different transmission speed. The signals from nervous system stimulates the endocrine system, which inturn target the specific organ to function.
Related Theory
Along with the nervous system, the endocrine system coordinates the body's functions to maintain homeostasis during rest and exercise. The nervous and endocrine systems also work together to initiate and control movement, and all the physiological processes movement involves.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Bowman's glands are found in:
questions.solution:
Bowman's glands are situated in the olfactory mucosa, beneath the olfactory epithelium, in the lamina propria, a connective tissue also containing fibroblasts, blood vessels, and bundles of fine axons from the olfactory neurons.
Related Theory
Bowman's capsule is a part of the nephron that forms a cup-like sack surrounding the glomerulus. It serves as a filter to remove organic wastes, excess inorganic salts, and water.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Parkinson's disease (characterized by tremors and progressive rigidity of limbs) is caused by degeneration of brain neurons that are involved in movement control and make use of neurotransmitter:
questions.solution:
Parkinson's disease is a degenerative, progressive disorder that affects nerve cells in deep parts of the brain called the basal ganglia and the substantia nigra. Nerve cells in the substantia nigra produce the neurotransmitter dopamine and are responsible for relaying messages that plan and control body movement.
Related Theory
Dopamine plays important roles in executive function, motor control, motivation, arousal, reinforcement, and reward through signaling cascades that are exerted via binding to dopaminergic receptors.
Caution
Dopamine system is linked to motivation. Serotonin is involved in emotions, which can affect your overall mood.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: In a man, abducens nerve is injured. Which one of the following functions will be affected?
questions.solution:
The abducens nerve is the sixth paired cranial nerve. It has a purely somatic motor function-providing innervation to the lateral rectus muscle responsible for outward gaze.
Related Theory
Six cranial nerves innervate motor, sensory, and autonomic structures in the eyes. The six cranial nerves are the optic nerve (CN II), oculomotor nerve (CN III), trochlear nerve (CN IV), trigeminal nerve (CN V), abducens nerve (CN VI), and facial nerve (CN VII).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Four healthy people in their twenties got involved in injuries resulting in damage and death of few cells of the following.
Which of the cell, are least likely to be replaced by new cells?
questions.solution:
Nerve cells are unable to divide because they lack centrioles, which plays important role in cell division. Centrioles help to arrange the microtubules that move chromosomes during cell division to ensure each daughter cell receives the appropriate number of chromosomes. While all other cells in our body have capacity to regenerate/self-repair.
Related Theory
Our brain is evolved to process complex tasks at a higher pace than other living beings. The brain achieves this with help of the whole nervous system, which is based on interneuronal connections, so adding an extra neuron would mess up these connections and alter both the functionality and the "stored" information. New cells in the nervous system wouldn't do any good. Thus, we lack of regenerative capacity of neurons.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: One of the examples of the action of the autonomous nervous system is:
questions.solution:
The autonomic nervous system regulates involuntary physiologic processes including heart rate, blood pressure, respiration, digestion, and sexual arousal. It contains three anatomically distinct divisions: sympathetic, parasympathetic and enteric. A reflex action, also known as a reflex, is an involuntary and nearly instantaneous movement in response to a stimulus. A reflex does not require any thought input. Peristalsis of intestine is related with autonomous nervous system whereas knee-jerk response, pupillary reflex and swallowing of food are reflex action.
Related Theory
The path taken by the nerve impulses in a reflex is called a reflex arc. In higher animals, most sensory neurons do not pass directly into the brain, but synapse in the spinal cord. This characteristic allows reflex actions to occur relatively quickly by activating spinal motor neurons without the delay of routing signals through the brain, although the brain will receive sensory input while the reflex action occurs.
A Caution
Autonomic nervous system is regulated by CNS while reflex action is controlled by spinal nerves

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Injury to vagus nerve in humans is not likely to affect:
questions.solution:
Vagus nerve, cranial nerve $\mathrm{X}$ is the longest cranial nerve which runs from the brain through the face and thorax to the abdomen. It is a mixed nerve that contains parasympathetic fibres.
Related Theory

Related Theory
The sodium-potassium pump is a mechanism of active transport that moves sodium ions out of cells and potassium ions into cells. The sodium-potassium pump moves both ions from areas of lower to higher concentration, using energy in ATP and carrier proteins in the cell membrane. Sodium is the principal ion in the fluid outside of cells, and potassium is the principal ion in the fluid inside of cells. These differences in concentration create an electrical gradient across the cell membrane, called resting potential.

The nodes of Ranvier allow for ions to diffuse in and out of the neuron, propagating the electrical signal down the axon. questions.solution: In non-myelinated nerve fibres, the ionic changes are repeated over the membrane all along the length of the fibre. So, the action potential flows all along the membrane over the entire length of the fibre. But in myelinated fibres, the ionic changes and the consequent depolarisation can take place only at the nodes of Ranvier free from myelin sheath, because the myelin sheath between the nodes insulates the fibre and prevents its depolarisation. So, the action potential in effect jumps from one node to the next.This is called saltatory conduction of nerve impulses. Because of this, nerve impulses do not have to run all along the myelinated nerve fibre. This is why nerve impulses are conducted far more rapidly in myelinated fibres than in the non - myelinated ones.

questions.solution:
Glaucoma is a condition in which loss of vision occurs because of an abnormally high pressure in the eye. In most cases there is no other ocular disease. This is known as primary glaucoma and there are two pathologically distinct types- acute and chronic simple. In acute (or angle-closure) glaucoma, there is an abrupt rise in pressure due to sudden closure of the angle between the comea and iris where aqueous humour usually drains from the eye. This is accompanied by pain and marked blurring of vision associated with inflammation of the anterior segment. In the more common chronic simple (or open-angle) glaucoma, the pressure increases gradually, usually without producing, pain, and the visual loss is insidious. The same type of visual loss may rarely occur in eyes with a normal pressure, this is called low-tension glaucoma.
Hepatitis is an inflammation of the liver caused by viruses, toxic substances or immunological abnormalities. Measles (Rubeola disease) is an acute infectious eruptive viral disease of childhood (3-5 years old) caused by specific virus of the group myxoviruses. Basically it is caused by an RNA containing Rubeola virus/Polynosa morbillorum. Measles is the infection of respiratory tract and conjunctiva which is transmitted by contact, fomite and droplet methods. Bronchitis is the inflammation of the bronchi.

questions.solution:
During the propagation of nerve impulse when a stimulus of adequate strength is applied to a polarized membrane, the permeability of the membrane to $\mathrm{Na}^{+}$is greatly increased at the point of stimulatioin. As a result, the sodium ion channels permit the influx of $\mathrm{Na}^{+}$by diffusion. Since, there are more $\mathrm{Na}^{+}$ions entering than leaving, the electrical potential of the membrane changes from -70 mV towards zero.
At 0 mV the membrane is said to be depolarized. While the resting potential is determined largely by $\mathrm{K}^{+}$ions, the action potential is determined largely by $\mathrm{Na}^{+}$ions. Action potential is another name of nerve impulse. The stimulated negatively charged point on the outside of the membrane sends out an electrical current to the positive point adjacent to it. questions.solution: Two types of photoreceptor cells are present in retina, ie, rods and cones. (i) Rods: These cells are active in dark Rhodopsin, a vision pigment is present in rods. In strong light, rhodopsin is bleached due to splitting of its two components, ie, scotopsin and retinal. But is reformed in dim light, ie, dark. (ii)Cones: These cells are active in strong light. Iodopsin a pigment is present in cones. These cells produce hare coloured image in bright light.

questions.q: In parasympathetic nervous system, which of the following is released?
questions.solution: Autonomic Nervous System (ANS) automatically regulates the activities of smooth muscles, cardiac muscles and glands. This coordination is involuntary. Autonomic nervous system consists of two divisions :(i) Sympathetic ANS : It shows sympathy, ie, generally increases the function and expenditure of energy takes place. Preganglionic nerve secretes acetylcholine and postganglionic nerve secrete "sympathatin" (norepinephrine). (ii) Parasympathetic ANS : It provides relaxation, comfort, pleasure at the time of rest and conservation of energy takes place. Postganglionic nerve secretes acetylcholine. Serotonin is a vasoconstrictor, secreted from mast cells.

questions.q: In a man, abducens nerve is injured. Which one of the following functions will be affected?
questions.solution: Abducens (abducent) nerve is a cranial nerve, which originated from the ventral surface of medulla oblongata. It innervates the lateral rectus muscle of eye ball. It is a motor nerve and controls the movements of the eye ball. Hence, if abducens nerve is injured in a man, movement of eye ball will be affected.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: If dorsal nerve of spinal cord is broken down then its effect is :
questions.solution: Spinal nerve is a mixed nerve which arises from grey matter of spinal cord. Spinal nerves have two roots. The dorsal root is sensory and the ventral root is motor. If dorsal nerve of spinal cord is broken down, the pathway of nerve will break, so, no impulse will transmitted.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Schwann cell is found around
questions.solution: All multicellular animals contain elongated nerve cells, called neurons. Each neuron has a cell body, axon and smaller processes called dendrites. An axon is the process of a nerve cell that carries impulses away from it. Axons run parallel to one another and each is surrounded along its whole length by series of Schwann cells. They may have myelin sheath.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which part of retina consists of only cones?
questions.solution: Lateral to the blind spot, there is a dipressed area of the retina, called fovea centralis, which contains only cones. Ability for vision is highest in the fovea.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Reflex action involves
questions.solution: Reflexes are classified as the spinal reflexes and the cranial reflexes. The former are so called because their basic neural path leads through spinal nerves and spinal cord. Reflexes at the spinal level have the purpose of removing the animal from harmful stimuli.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Ventricles are related to
questions.solution: Ventricles are related to both heart and brain. Mammalian heart is four chambered. The upper two chambers known as right and left auricle and the lower as right and left ventricles. In brain there are four ventricles. Ventricle Ist and II (lateral ventricles) are cavities of two cerebral hemispheres. IIIrd ventricle (diocoel) is cavity of diencephalon and IV ventricle (metacoel) is cavity of medulla oblongata.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following is the part of mid brain of rabbit?
questions.solution: The dorsal part of mid brain (mesencephalon) is in the form of two pairs (i.e., four) of spherical optic lobes (corpora quadrigemina) located behind the pineal body optic lobes are reduced merely as reflex centres of visual and auditory.

questions.q: Organ of Corti is found in
questions.solution: Organ of Corti are found in cochlear channel (internal ear) and are responsible for hearing. Ear is concerned both with hearing and balance, semicircular canals are responsible for balance when body is in motion.
